project.title: SARS-CoV-2 PLpro deISGylation of host proteins

experiment.title: HeLa ISG15 knockout shotgun proteomics of the GG-enrichment input, IFN-alpha then lysate PLpro wild-type vs mutant

rationale: The shotgun (total-proteome) arm of PXD026748, curated as its own record because one record carries one file and one content_hash. (1) The column-to-condition mapping is read from the twelve per-run LFQ intensity column names, which follow the raw filenames: after 'shotgun-', 'ctrl' is taken as the HeLa wild-type genotype and 'ko' as ISG15-/-, the following 'wt' or 'mut' as wild-type or mutant PLpro, and the trailing '-N' as the replicate index. The naming differs from the GG arm's ('Gly-Gly-WT'/'Gly-Gly-KO', '_mut', '_repN'), so the correspondence between the two arms' condition labels is itself an inference from filenames; basis is 'filename_inference' and I8 forbids presenting it as the submitters'. (2) The material is read from the publication (Munnur et al., Nat Immunol 22:1416-1427, 2021, Methods, 'Sample preparation for PLpro ISGylome'), not from the PRIDE record, which describes only the GG workflow: after PLpro treatment and on-column trypsin digestion of each replicate, 'an aliquot of 30 µg total peptide was taken for shotgun proteomics analysis' and the remainder went to GG immunocapture. Each shotgun run therefore measures an unenriched aliquot of the same digest one GG run measures after enrichment. (3) Per ADR-0035 R1 (Proposed) a Sample is the material measured, so these are twelve Samples distinct from the GG record's. Their biology fields are deliberately identical to the GG record's, because the material is the same up to the split; they are distinct because Sample identity is anchored on Experiment and this record's experiment has its own title and modality 'proteomics'. Copying the GG record's experiment block would merge all twelve Samples into the GG record's, which a test pins against. (4) The mapping keys are the LFQ intensity family, so the ingestion declares quantity 'lfq' (quantity_from_mapping_keys): the publication's own shotgun analysis consumed LFQ intensities. Since 2026-09-19 (turn 10d) the protein-groups adapter retains every family the file reports, and this file reports three families of twelve per-run columns each (Intensity, LFQ intensity, iBAQ), so the declaration fixes the key family and the recorded quantity, not what is stored. (5) Search parameters are from the file's parameters.txt and summary.txt in the deposit's 20210616_Shotgun_PRIDE.zip: MaxQuant 1.6.17.0, a single FASTA UP000005640_9606.fasta under a folder dated 01_2021, match between runs off. The publication gives the instrument (Q Exactive HF) and data-dependent acquisition for the GG runs, and says the shotgun aliquots ran on the same LC-MS/MS system with similar settings. File identity: proteinGroups.txt is the zip member of that name, 11,174,233 bytes; its sha256 was computed on 2026-09-19 twice on bzk's machine, from the member read inside the zip and from the unzipped copy, with the same result (notes/scripts/inspect_shotgun.py and shasum).
unresolved: DIGEST SPLIT — each shotgun Sample and one GG Sample are portions of one replicate's digest (the Methods sentence quoted in the rationale). The schema has no relation between Samples (bzk/ontology/schema.py's relationship tables name none), which is ADR-0035 R2's unrepresentable relation in a second form: a split of one digest across two measurements rather than a blocking pair of conditions. Consequence: a protein-abundance adjustment of GG sites can be keyed in the graph at condition grain only; a sample-grain adjustment has no recorded link to key on.

REPLICATE LABELS — the 'replicate' values 1-3 here are this arm's labels, read from the '-N' suffixes. Which shotgun '-N' came from the same digest as which GG '_repN' is not stated anywhere in the deposit or the publication. Consequence: equal replicate values across the two records must not be read as pairing. A join on condition plus replicate asserts a correspondence nothing records, and ADR-0035 R2 already says 'replicate' does not carry one.

RUN LAYOUT — read from the run names: the shotgun runs were acquired in condition blocks by run number (77-81 ctrl_wt, 83-87 ctrl_mut, 89-93 ko_wt, 95-99 ko_mut), and the three ko_mut runs alone carry 'WNE14_trap5' where the other nine carry 'WNE2_trap4' or 'WNE3_trap4'. All twelve GG runs carry 'WNE14_trap5' with conditions interleaved in run order. Measured on bzk's machine 2026-09-19 by notes/scripts/coverage_shotgun.py over the 4,768 groups remaining after decoy and contaminant removal: groups with a non-zero Intensity per ko_mut run were 3,421, 4,126 and 3,941, against at most 3,623 in any other run; groups with Intensity but no LFQ value were 1,227, 1,478 and 1,330, against at most 1,125 in any other run. Reading 'trap' as the LC trap column is a judgement. Consequence: any ko_mut difference at protein grain is confounded with run block and possibly with hardware, and the pattern of missing values is condition-linked, so an imputation over this arm would fill the ko_mut block differently from the rest.

GLYGLY IN THE SHOTGUN SEARCH — summary.txt lists 'GlyGly (K)' among the shotgun search's variable modifications, and 98 GlyGly-carrying forms appear in modificationSpecificPeptides.txt. The publication says the GG modification was added for the GG-peptidomics samples and is silent about the shotgun search: a contradiction by implication, not by explicit statement. The deposit governs. parameters.txt excludes such peptides from protein quantification ('Use only unmodified peptides and' True; included modifications Oxidation (M) and Acetyl (Protein N-term); 'Discard unmodified counterpart peptides' True). A check on 2026-09-19 by notes/scripts/check_intensity.py found proteinGroups Intensity equal to the GlyGly-excluded razor-peptide sum in 32 of 34 discriminating group-runs and equal to the all-forms sum alone in none, with a control of 38,327 of 41,544 group-runs matching. Consequence: the protein values do not carry the shotgun search's GlyGly signal, so they can serve as a protein baseline for GG sites without circularity, bounded by that n of 34.

PROTEIN COUNT — the file has 4,916 protein-group rows; 148 carry Reverse (62) or Potential contaminant (86), none both, leaving 4,768. Of these, 4,709 have Intensity in at least one run and 3,131 have LFQ intensity in at least one run. The publication states 3,130 identified proteins with at least one unique or razor peptide. The nearest count is 3,131, but the two may not measure the same thing; the gap of 1 is recorded and no rule was searched to close it. Consequence: the file's population and the publication's are not reconciled.

FILTERS — the publication removed proteins only identified by site. The file has 93 such rows; 20 of them are also Reverse or Potential contaminant and are dropped with those, so 73 reach the graph. Corrected 2026-09-19: this item first said the ingested ProteinObservations 'include those 93', which assumed no overlap with the dropped rows and was never measured; the overlap was measured by notes/scripts/measure_shotgun_ingest.py against walk/PREREG-PXD026748-shotgun-ingest.md #10. The protein-groups adapter filters Reverse and Potential contaminant only. Consequence: ingested ProteinObservations include those 73, and any comparison with the publication's shotgun analysis must remove them explicitly.

QUANTITY COVERAGE — 1,578 of the 4,709 (notes/scripts/coverage_shotgun.py) groups with Intensity in some run never receive an LFQ value; the file's quantification setting is 'Peptides used for protein quantification' Unique. Consequence: a protein baseline computed over the declared LFQ family covers fewer groups than one over Intensity. Both are stored. Changing the declared family means changing this record's mapping keys, which moves the ingestion Analysis id and nothing else.

PROVENANCE OF R1 — the Sample convention applied here comes from ADR-0035, which is Proposed. curation_PXD026748.json applies the same convention. Consequence: if R1 changes at review, both PXD026748 records are revisited together.
